item.title: gRPC-Go RBAC Authorization Bypass via Missing Leading Slash in `:path` (CVE-2026-33186)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System google.golang.org/grpc (grpc-go) authz package (SDK-level RBAC)
Versions Affected grpc-go < v1.79.3 (fixed in v1.79.3, PR #8981)
Language / Platform Python 3.8+ PoC using raw HTTP/2 frames against a Go gRPC server
Authentication Required No
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

gRPC-Go’s authz package implements RBAC using deny/allow rules matched against the HTTP/2 :path pseudo-header (e.g. /Service/Method). The HTTP/2 server transport stores the raw, pre-normalization :path value in context, but the routing layer (handleStream) normalizes the path (adding a leading slash) before dispatch. Because the RBAC engine reads the value via grpc.Method(ctx) — the pre-normalization form — a deny rule written as /Service/Method fails to match a request sent with :path = "Service/Method" (no leading slash), since the comparison mismatches on the first character. The default allow policy then fires and the protected method executes. Any server using authz.NewStatic() or authz.NewFileWatcher() with deny rules is affected, and exploitation only requires a raw HTTP/2 client capable of sending a custom :path value.
